conviction_note: First print as a standalone company. The quarter is the seasonal trough (H2 is about 12-13% of annual seed EBITDA) and consensus already expects a larger operating loss than last year (-$300m against -$193m). What I found is small and offsets: Brazil first-crop corn area +10.7% and peer LatAm seed growth on the plus side, a tough Q3 2025 comp (early LatAm deliveries) and a consensus slightly above the ~$2.8B 2026 EBITDA guide on the minus side. abs_move 4.5 comes from 36.9% realised vol plus a first-print premium (consolidated Corteva accounting, possible 2027 commentary, litigation Q&A). p_up 50 because nothing decides the sign.
bar: Q3 2026 seed-only consensus: net sales $918.1m, EBITDA -$299.8m, EBIT -$602.7m, net income -$687m (about -$1.03/sh on 667.3m shares) per MarketScreener (https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/VYLOR-INC-217063745/finances/). Futu's preview carries the same $918.06m revenue and -$1.03 EPS (https://news.futunn.com/en/post/1003636645/earnings-preview-vylor-inc-to-report-financial-results-post-market, via search snippet), so the two sources likely share one feed. KeyCorp's EPS is -$0.49 (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/10/09/what-is-keycorps-forecast-for-vylor-q3-earnings.html), so the EPS bar is disputed. Basis risk: the NT 10-Q says Vylor's Q3 statements will be Corteva's CONSOLIDATED interim statements, seed plus crop protection, because Vylor is the accounting spinnor (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2128626/000119312526455591/d107437dnt10q.htm). The seed-only bar is therefore not like for like with the GAAP headline. Prior-year comp: Q3 2025 seed net sales $917m, seed operating EBITDA -$193m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1755672/000175567225000020/a3q_2025xearningsxnewsxr.htm). FY2026 guide is about $10.4bn sales and $2.8bn operating EBITDA (27% margin), from the Sept 15 Investor Day as reported in https://everyspinofff.substack.com/p/every-spin-off-8-vylor-and-new-corteva. FY2026 EBITDA consensus is $2,830m (MarketScreener). Because the EPS bar is disputed and the basis is mixed, every size is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 14.99m shares = 2.25% of shares outstanding, short ratio 1.79 days (stockanalysis.com statistics, page updated 2026-11-11, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/vylr/statistics/). Not a crowded short. Skew: baseline skew_25d_vol_points null, chain unusable (ATM spread 93% of mid). Put/call OI 0.49 on only 961 contracts, so the option market makes no directional statement. Tape: spot 71.43, -4.0% over 20d, +0.25% over 5d, 7.2% below the 52w high. Valuation stretched against the remaining company: about 17x next-year EBITDA, and the seed business is about 86% of the combined post-spin value (substack, 2026-10-27). Sell-side average target $82-83, 16 analysts, mostly Buy, initiations dated early October. S&P 500 seat taken over from Corteva on day one (New Corteva moved to MidCap 400 on Oct 6), so the index flow is done.

findings.finding: Vylor filed an NT 10-Q on 2026-11-10. It says Q3 statements will be Corteva's consolidated interim statements (Vylor is the accounting successor) and that it 'expects a higher seasonal loss as compared to the same period in 2025', due to separation activities and ongoing R&D investment. No figures are given. Consensus seed EBITDA of -$300m against -$193m a year ago already embeds a loss about $107m worse, so the direction is expected and the magnitude is not stated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No standalone history (0 prior 8-K 2.02 prints in the baseline). As Corteva, the Q2 2026 print raised the FY guide and the shares still fell on a revenue shortfall (https://www.agnavigator.com/Article/2026/08/03/corteva-lifts-outlook-but-investors-want-more-than-margin-growth-ahead-of-split/), so the top line has mattered more than seasonal margin.
findings.why_not_priced: Filed the evening before the print and carries no numbers. It is on stocktitan, but if the market had read it as a warning, the 5-day tape would not sit at +0.25%. Most of the separation cost falls outside non-GAAP operating EBITDA, which is the line the bar is set on, so the GAAP 'higher loss' is mostly below the line the stock trades on.
findings.independence: The consensus EBITDA of -$300m against Q3 2025's -$193m points the same way (a larger loss expected), from MarketScreener and Corteva's Q3 2025 release. These are different documents.

findings.finding: Latin America drives Q3 seed volume (Q3 2025 LatAm seed sales were $391m of $917m, +79%, helped by early deliveries ahead of safrinha), and the read for Q3 2026 is mixed. For: Conab's first 2026/27 survey (2026-10-15) has Brazil first-crop corn area +10.7% to 4.54m ha and total corn area +4.9%, and Bayer's Q3 LatAm sales rose 5.6% on summer-season corn and soy seed demand. Against: the Q3 2025 pull-forward makes a tough comp, and consensus sales are flat at $918m against $917m. Net, a mild positive for the sales line against a flat bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No standalone history. In Corteva's Q3 2025, a +33% seed sales quarter driven by LatAm early deliveries came with a raised FY guide; that was a consolidated-company reaction and not this ticker.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue sits exactly flat on last year ($918m against $917m), as if neither the area expansion nor the tough comp had been modelled. Had analysts priced the summer-corn area gain, the bar would sit above last year. Had they priced the pull-forward comp, it would sit below. It is a proxy, and the company has not confirmed it.
findings.independence: Peer read: Bayer Q3 2026 LatAm +5.6% on summer seed demand, corn seed flat; Syngenta seed flat with Brazil growth offset by lower US corn acres (https://www.global-agriculture.com/crop-protection/q3-2026-agribusiness-results-seeds-hold-firm-as-crop-protection-slides/, 2026-11-06). Q3 2025 comp: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1755672/000175567225000020/a3q_2025xearningsxnewsxr.htm. Three different documents, all proxies apart from the company's own prior-year number.

findings.finding: The GAAP Q3 statements will be consolidated Corteva, seed plus crop protection (NT 10-Q). The street bar is seed-only ($918m sales), while Q3 2025 consolidated Corteva sales were roughly 2.5-3x the seed figure. Headline feeds may print a large 'revenue beat' and a smaller loss per share against the seed-only -$1.03, and the EPS bar is already split (-$0.49 KeyCorp against -$1.03 consensus). This is a mechanical after-hours tailwind that should fade by the first full session once segment and pro forma tables are read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history for this name. Spin-off first prints with mixed reporting bases often whipsaw in after-hours. No sourced example for this ticker.
findings.why_not_priced: The aggregator previews (Futu, MarketScreener) still carry a seed-only bar with no note on the reporting basis. Had the basis been priced, previews would quote a pro forma bar or a consolidated one. This is an inference about the headline mechanics, not about fundamentals, and it is sized small because the exit is the next close, not the after-hours.
findings.independence: Shares the NT 10-Q with finding 1 (one document, two different lines: the loss direction against the reporting basis). The bar split comes from https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/10/09/what-is-keycorps-forecast-for-vylor-q3-earnings.html.

findings.finding: FY2026 seed operating EBITDA consensus is $2,830m, slightly above the 'about $2.8bn' the company gave at its Sept 15 Investor Day. H1 seed EBITDA was already $3.0bn (Corteva Q2 release), so H2 has to come in at about -$0.2bn. Reaffirming at $2.8bn would leave a hair of downside to the street, all inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As Corteva in Q2 2026, a raised guide did not stop a decline, so this shareholder base has not paid for guide moves alone. No standalone history.
findings.why_not_priced: The gap is 1% of the annual number, which is the kind of discrepancy consensus databases carry after a spin until the first print resets them. If it were priced, consensus would sit at or below $2.8bn. It lands inside what the company guided, so it is near zero.
findings.independence: Consensus figure from https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/VYLOR-INC-217063745/finances/. H1 seed EBITDA $3.0bn from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001755672/000175567226000022/a2q_2026xearningsxnewsxr.htm.

outside_window.finding: Multistate PFAS fraudulent-transfer suit against EIDP, Corteva and Vylor (State of Indiana v. EIDP, 7th Cir. No. 26-3075). The TRO on dividends and buybacks was stayed pending appeal by the Seventh Circuit on 2026-10-20 (split decision), and the merits appeal is pending with appellees' brief due about 2026-11-23. A merits ruling or new injunction would be material either way but is not scheduled inside the window.

baseline_tension: The baseline is thin (no history, unusable chain, no skew), so there is no market lean to agree or disagree with; the mild -4% 20-day drift and a stretched multiple against small, offsetting findings argue for a coin flip on the sign.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): the EPS bar is disputed (-$0.49 against -$1.03) and the reporting basis is mixed, so every finding stays capped small. The guidance finding lands inside the guide, -0.2 to -0.1.
Rule 1 / core table (finding inside what the company signalled): the NT 10-Q 'higher seasonal loss' is already embedded in consensus, -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 5 (proxy smaller): the LatAm area and peer read is a proxy the company has not confirmed, +0.3 to +0.2. The headline-basis item is an inference, +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 7: short interest checked (2.25%, 1.79 days), not crowded. No skew to beat. abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged.
